paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM, and four SepLLM configurations. The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration", has a linear scale, and ranges from 0 to 140,000 with a tick label interval of 20,000. The y-axis is labeled "Loss", has a linear scale, and ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with a tick label interval of 0.1. The plot displays six lines, each representing a different model configuration: Vanilla (purple, solid line), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, solid line), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid line), and SepLLM (n=128) (dark blue, solid line). All lines start above 3.3 and decrease rapidly within the first 20,000 iterations, with the Vanilla model decreasing from approximately 3.35 to 2.7, StrmLLM (n=64) from 3.36 to 2.8, SepLLM (n=64) from 3.34 to 2.65, SepLLM (n=64, H) from 3.33 to 2.65, SepLLM (n=64, H/T) from 3.33 to 2.65, and SepLLM (n=128) from 3.37 to 2.75. By 140,000 iterations, the lines continue to decrease at a slower rate, with the Vanilla model reaching approximately 2.45, StrmLLM (n=64) reaching around 2.6, SepLLM (n=64) reaching about 2.51, SepLLM (n=64, H) reaching approximately 2.52, SepLLM (n=64, H/T) reaching around 2.49, and SepLLM (n=128) reaching about 2.55.
